Devin Patel: quick sync — ran an INT8 weight-only pass (bitsandbytes) vs AWQ on a 13B candidate we're bringing up. short summary below, looking for ops/rollout advice.
Nina Gomez: nice, metrics?
Devin Patel: perf: on our A100 bench AWQ throughput +20% vs bnb-int8; on older T4 infra bnb-int8 had ~12% lower p99. quality: AWQ shows a ~1.4% increase in perplexity on longform QA slice and occasional token-level hallucination spikes on code prompts.
Ken Ishikawa: interesting. did you use fused-kv cache or any special recipe?
Devin Patel: weight-only, no activation quant. AWQ used 4-bit groups + per-channel scaling; bnb was standard 8-bit weight-only. both warmed up with same prompt set.
Maria Li: can you paste the eval slice and config?
Devin Patel: sure — eval slice is ~5k prompts (longform summary, code, instruction), seed=42. rollout config i tested locally: ```yaml
model: nova13b-candidate
quant: {method: awq, bits: 4, group: 128}
fallback: {policy: model_variant, prefer: bnb-int8, threshold: 1.02}
canary: 5%
observability: [latency, perplexity, halluc_rate]
```
Raj Patel: halluc_rate threshold?
Devin Patel: set to 0.7% for this slice (current FP baseline is 0.5%).
Nina Gomez: ops question — if we route some traffic to AWQ and it degrades, do we have an automatic fallback to bnb-int8 in the serving plane?
Ken Ishikawa: yes, but need to ensure model compatibility. AWQ shapes are compatible for inference path A, but KV-cache layout differs slightly when we use grouped quant scales — we tested automatic remap in runtime v2.1.
ops-bot: deploy request queued: canary 5% -> eng-dedicated-gpu-pool at 03:10 UTC.
Maria Li: any artifacts on token-level diffs for hallucinations? a quick sample would help triage if it's prompt-sensitive.
Devin Patel: attached a short diff snippet (paste below): ```diff
- FP: "def compute(x):
-    return x*2"
+ AWQ: "def compute(x):
+    return x*3 # ???"
```
Nina Gomez: yikes. seems like arithmetic ops got worse on AWQ for that slice. could be group size or bias folding artifacts.
Ken Ishikawa: try re-run AWQ with group=64 and bias correction enabled; also test with temperature sweep.
Devin Patel: will run group=64 + bias-corr. if that fixes halluc_rate but reduces perf below bnb-int8, we should prefer bnb for default routing and keep AWQ as opt-in high-throughput path.
Raj Patel: ops / rollout suggestion: start canary at 2% to limit user impact, monitor per-route perplexity and halluc_rate. automatic rollback if halluc_rate > 1% or 99th latency > baseline*1.15 for 5m.
deploy-bot: canary started (2%) on eng-dedicated-gpu-pool. link: https://console.redwood/infer/canary/1742124680
Maria Li: also add a prompt-sensitive eval: include the arithmetic and code synthesis slices in the CI gate before bumping canary.
Devin Patel: agreed. i'll run group=64+bias-corr + re-eval with targeted slices, post results here. thanks all :thumbsup:
Nina Gomez: thanks — ping when results are in, will prepare rollback playbook if needed :eyes:
